newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures down on profit-taking.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE was down at Tokyo midday on Thursday, pushed lower by profit-taking sales, traders said.
The June contract ended the morning session down 0.03 at 99.19, after moving between 99.18 and 99.22.

"After two days of rises, some players were creating new short positions, while those with longs were taking profits. So the June's upside seems limited at around today's intraday high for the time being," said a trader at a city bank.
The volume of the June contract was 44,851 contracts.

Selling by foreign accounts were seen in Euroyen futures and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures at mid-morning, due to speculation that the Japanese government would set up a body similar to the U.S. Resolution Trust Corp (RTC) to facilitate bad loan write-offs by banks, traders said.
Bank analysts, however, said it was highly unlikely that Japan's Ministry of Finance and municipal governments, which supervise regional financial institutions, would agree to such a framework.
The key December JGB futures contract was up 0.19 at 124.53 at midday, off its intraday high of 124.71.
In the interbank call market, the key unsecured overnight call money was earlier traded at 0.49 percent, but later fell to 0.48 percent.
On Wednesday, the weighted average of the overnight rate edged up to 0.49 percent due to fund demand related to tax payments, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 500 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
The key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.51 percent, down from 0.52 percent on Wednesday. -- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
